newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends up sharply on funds, Egypt talk.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends up sharply on funds, Egypt talk.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled broadly higher on a mixture of fund buying and talk that Egypt may be preparing to buy a large chunk of U.S. wheat, traders said.

"We had big fund short covering in Chicago and, to a lesser extent, here," a KCBT trader said. "There was also a rumor that Egypt was in for (up to 750,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat) for Sept/Oct delivery."
But U.S. grain exporters told Reuters they had received no indications that Egypt would announce a tender, and most said they did not expect one this week.
Traders said the fund short covering was ushered in after an early wave of commercial-related buying.

The higher performance defied opening calls, which were for KCBT wheat to open mixed and stay choppy in what traders expected would be a consolidation ahead of the Friday release of USDA's July crop report.
KCBT wheat settled five to 10-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with September up 10 cents at $3.39-1/2. July gained 10-1/2 cents to close at $3.33-1/2.

Refco was a featured player, picking up 2.6 million Sept bushels but also selling 1.1 million Sept. ADM's Benson-Quinn unit bought two million Sept and one million December bushels, but also sold one million Sept and 1.5 million Dec.
